name: SampleRateTap (async engine)
baseline: libsamplerate 0.2.2 (Secret Rabbit Code, MEDIUM and BEST converters)
workload: Asynchronous near-unity sample rate conversion (two clock domains) measured as million output frames per second for mono, stereo and 8-channel streams at a matched ~120 dB and ~140 dB stopband tier, plus algorithmic latency and embedded instruction counts.
claimed_speedup: Doc states SampleRateTap is 3.1-3.9x (stereo/mono; 1.5x at 8 channels) faster than libsamplerate at the matched ~120 dB tier and 6.1x at ~140 dB, with 2-3.6x less latency. Table: stereo 14.6 vs 4.8 Mframes/s (balanced vs libsamplerate MEDIUM), mono 20.3 vs 5.2, 8-ch 3.0 vs 1.9; ~140 dB stereo 9.6 vs 1.6 (BEST). The same table shows soxr HQ at 52.9 and r8brain-free-src at 16.5 stereo, i.e. it is SLOWER than soxr and r8brain on x86 host throughput.
compiler_and_flags: GCC 13.3 -O3 (CMake Release); libsamplerate 0.2.2 and soxr 0.1.3 Ubuntu 24.04 packages; r8brain at pinned commit 7.5 with Ooura FFT
hardware: shared Xeon @ 2.10 GHz (exact model not stated), run 2026-09-25; embedded rows use QEMU instruction counting for Cortex-M33 and Hexagon
tradeoffs: Specialised: near-unity asynchronous ratio (+-1000 ppm default) for clock-domain bridging, not a general-ratio resampler. Header-only C++20. Fixed-point Q15/Q31 paths for FPU-less DSPs. Very low latency (0.5 ms filter, 1.5 ms default).
caveats: Only beats libsamplerate; the same page shows soxr HQ (52.9 stereo) and r8brain (16.5 stereo) faster on x86 host throughput, which the author states openly. Measured on a shared Xeon with exact CPU model missing and ratios said to be the meaningful figures; libsamplerate latency rows were measured on 2026-06-12. Benchmark code is in the repo behind TAP_SR_BUILD_COMPARE_BENCH (off by default). Very young repo (commits Sep 30 to Oct 3 2026 visible, 225 commits), 5 stars; the benchmark page was written by the project author (first-party).

name: libfoxenflac
baseline: flac reference decoder application (Xiph flac / libFLAC)
workload: FLAC decoding on x86_64; README does not state the file, flags or timing method.
claimed_speedup: "reasonably fast, being about 25% faster than the flac reference decoder application on x86_64 systems"; performance on ARM6 "significantly worse".
tradeoffs: Tiny C99 decoder with no libc dependency and no heap allocation (8.8 kiB of WebAssembly); callable from C++. No seeking, no metadata other than STREAMINFO, no frame-header access. Decoder only (no encoder).
caveats: Single sentence in the README, no numbers beyond '25%', no benchmark code, no hardware, compiler or flags stated. The baseline is the flac command-line decoder application (includes its I/O and output handling), not libFLAC's API in isolation. Author says the code is not optimised and ARM6 is much slower. Last commit March 2025 (README fix).

name: libsoxr (SoX Resampler)
baseline: libsamplerate 0.2.2 (Secret Rabbit Code, MEDIUM and BEST converters)
workload: Sample rate conversion measured as million output frames per second for mono, stereo and 8-channel streams at a matched ~120 dB tier (soxr HQ vs libsamplerate MEDIUM) and ~140 dB tier (soxr VHQ vs libsamplerate BEST), run by a third-party author who compares his own resampler against both.
claimed_speedup: Third-party table (Mframes/s, higher is better): stereo ~120 dB tier soxr HQ 52.9 vs libsamplerate MEDIUM 4.8 (about 11x, derived from page data); mono 114.3 vs 5.2 (about 22x, derived); 8-ch 12.9 vs 1.9 (about 6.8x, derived); ~140 dB stereo soxr VHQ 32.1 vs libsamplerate BEST 1.6 (about 20x, derived). The page calls soxr the winner of raw host throughput.
compiler_and_flags: Benchmark harness built with GCC 13.3 -O3 (CMake Release); libsamplerate 0.2.2 and soxr 0.1.3 are the Ubuntu 24.04 distribution packages (their own build flags not stated)
hardware: shared Xeon @ 2.10 GHz (exact model not stated), median of 5, run 2026-09-25
stars_or_usage: 181 stars on this GitHub mirror; ships as a distribution package (Ubuntu 24.04 soxr 0.1.3)
tradeoffs: Large algorithmic latency (424-788 frames, 8.8-16.4 ms at HQ; 433 frames at VHQ) because it processes in big SIMD batches, so unsuitable for low-latency live monitoring; the benchmark author says so. LGPL-2.1. Offers a libsamplerate-like header (soxr-lsr.h) but not a full emulation.
caveats: The numbers come from a competitor's comparison page (SampleRateTap), not from the soxr project; the author benchmarks his own library and is open that soxr is faster than it on x86 host. CPU model is only 'shared Xeon @ 2.10 GHz'. Ratios are derived from page data. Supporting evidence in the python-soxr README (https://github.com/dofuuz/python-soxr, Colab notebook, CPU unspecified): 10 s of 48 kHz to 44.1 kHz in 10.8 ms (soxr HQ) vs 223 ms (samplerate sinc_medium) and 14.5 ms (VHQ) vs 794 ms (sinc_best), through Python bindings. The GitHub repo is a mirror; the canonical source is SourceForge, and the last commit on this mirror is 2018-02-24 (stable release, no development since). The patched fork dofuuz/soxr is maintained separately. The sibling file w10-av-gh-cpp.json already records libsoxr from the python-soxr README alone (tier C); this record adds an independent C/C++ measurement, so merge should keep the higher tier.

name: r8brain-free-src
baseline: libsamplerate 0.2.2 (Secret Rabbit Code, MEDIUM and BEST converters)
workload: Sample rate conversion measured as million output frames per second for mono, stereo and 8-channel streams at a matched ~120 dB tier (r8brain 120 dB preset vs libsamplerate MEDIUM) and ~140 dB tier (CDSPResampler16/24 vs libsamplerate BEST), run by a third-party author comparing his own resampler against it.
claimed_speedup: Third-party table (Mframes/s, higher is better): stereo ~120 dB r8brain 16.5 vs libsamplerate MEDIUM 4.8 (about 3.4x, derived from page data); mono 35.4 vs 5.2 (about 6.8x, derived); 8-ch 4.1 vs 1.9 (about 2.2x, derived); ~140 dB stereo CDSPResampler16 18.4 vs libsamplerate BEST 1.6 (about 11.5x, derived), CDSPResampler24 14.1 (about 8.8x, derived). The r8brain README itself states a rate of 38*n_cores Mrops (56*n_cores with Intel IPP) for 44100 to 96000 on a Ryzen 3700X but names no baseline.
compiler_and_flags: Benchmark harness built with GCC 13.3 -O3 (CMake Release); r8brain at the pinned commit (version 7.5) in stock configuration with the Ooura FFT; libsamplerate 0.2.2 is the Ubuntu 24.04 package
hardware: shared Xeon @ 2.10 GHz (exact model not stated), median of 5, run 2026-09-25
stars_or_usage: 743 stars; used in professional audio applications such as REAPER and Audirvana per the repo page
tradeoffs: Linear-phase FFT block convolution, so large latency (789 frames / 16.4 ms at the default 2% transition band, 1,700-1,782 frames at the 140 dB tier). Mono per instance, double precision I/O. Header-only, MIT. Optional Intel IPP or PFFFT FFT back ends for extra speed.
caveats: Numbers come from a competitor's comparison page, not from the r8brain project; the same table shows soxr HQ/VHQ about 1.7-3.2x faster than r8brain in every row (derived from page data). The benchmark used r8brain 7.5 with the Ooura FFT; the latest commit (2026-09-30, version 7.6) claims a 1.5-3x speedup of filter calculations on 64-bit platforms, so current numbers are likely better. CPU model only 'shared Xeon @ 2.10 GHz'. Ratios are derived from page data. The project's own README gives absolute rates only and says to make sure competing libraries are tuned for linear phase and similar stop-band.

name: minimp3
baseline: keyj's minimp3 (Martin J. Fiedler's fixed-point single-file MP3 decoder, https://keyj.emphy.de/minimp3/)
workload: Decoding the ISO/IEC 11172-4 and 13818-4 MP3 conformance vectors (compl.bit, he_*.bit, si*.bit, sin1k0db.bit); CPU clockticks measured with perf, I/O included.
claimed_speedup: README tables (clockticks, lower is better): compl.bit 14,306,684 vs 31,849,373 for keyj's minimp3 (about 2.2x fewer, derived from page data); he_44khz 21,296,300 vs 41,628,861 (about 2.0x, derived); hecommon 3,169,715 vs 20,437,779 (about 6.4x, derived); sin1k0db 24,842,977 vs 55,569,636 (about 2.2x, derived). Conformance: PSNR 107-144 dB for this minimp3 versus 0.15-72 dB for keyj's, which fails conformance on all vectors.
hardware: i7-6700K, speedstep effects avoided, measured with perf
tradeoffs: Single-header C decoder with SSE and NEON intrinsics, floating-point output; CC0 means no patent grant. The baseline is a fixed-point decoder with no vector code, so the comparison is between different design points.
caveats: Baseline is the original keyj minimp3, a small hobby decoder that does not pass conformance (PSNR below the 96 dB limit) and does not decode free-format streams, not libmpg123, libmad or FFmpeg's mp3 decoder; no comparison against any of those is published. Compiler and flags are not stated, numbers are first-party and from a 2015-era CPU (i7-6700K). The README says 'rough benchmark'. CC0-1.0 dedication carries no patent grant.
